name: Znect CI Bridge
description: In-development CircleCI read-only diagnostics bridge with a private authenticated Browser JSON API and bounded dashboard report export; optional MCP compatibility is not required for ChatGPT access.

intended: Browser dashboard and manual JSON report handoff
tested: Historical Worker tests and Preview smoke checks exist on earlier revisions; current feature-branch source has not yet been validated through central Znect Build.

permissions: Network access to the configured Cloudflare Worker and approved CircleCI API endpoints
Read-only CircleCI project/build data using a secret token
Primary ChatGPT handoff through the authenticated Browser JSON API using WEB_ACCESS_TOKEN
Optional separate MCP authentication using MCP_ACCESS_TOKEN; MCP is not required for Browser API access
dependencies: CircleCI API v3 (current), with legacy API v1.1 compatibility tools
MCP TypeScript server/client SDK 2.4.0 (optional compatibility interface; not required for ChatGPT Browser API access)
security_controls: Bearer authentication for /mcp with fixed-length digest comparison
Streamable HTTP Origin validation delegated to Cloudflare Agents SDK v2; rejects malformed, opaque, and untrusted browser origins
Registry-scoped CircleCI project paths and read-only GET requests
CircleCI redirect rejection and 15-second outbound request timeouts; artifact redirects are manually revalidated
HTTPS artifact URL allowlist and default-port restriction
Streaming log body byte ceiling
Per-action and aggregate log output character limits
Configured Worker secrets redacted from returned logs
Secrets supplied through Cloudflare Worker Secrets
CircleCI API JSON response body size ceiling
Nested workflow/job inspection and automatic diagnostics have explicit page, failed-job, log-action, and artifact budgets to remain below the 50-subrequest Workers Free ceiling
Maximum three allowlisted artifact redirects
Fail-closed HTTP 503 when rate limiting is missing or unavailable
Best-effort pattern redaction for common Bearer/Basic, GitHub/GitLab/Slack, Stripe, Google, npm, AWS, JWT, PEM, and key/value credential formats
Separate Bearer authentication for /mcp (MCP_ACCESS_TOKEN) and /api/v1/* (WEB_ACCESS_TOKEN)
Cloudflare Rate Limiting binding: 60 authenticated MCP and browser API requests per 60 seconds per Cloudflare location
Authenticated rate-limit keys are SHA-256 digests of their respective access tokens; raw tokens are not used as keys
Failed MCP and browser API authentication attempts use a separate SHA-256 client-IP digest bucket
CircleCI outbound webhook ingress verifies v1 HMAC-SHA256 signatures against the exact raw request body
Webhook events are correlated to API v3 runs only by exact commit revision, compatible branch, and bounded event/run execution interval; ambiguous candidates are not silently selected
Webhook payloads are capped at 64 KiB, filtered to CircleCI project slugs explicitly registered in the project registry, normalized to allowlisted fields, and deduplicated by CircleCI event ID
SQLite-backed Durable Object stores at most 500 normalized events and prunes events older than 30 days
limitations: The current feature-branch head has not been deployed to Preview or Production; earlier Preview smoke checks are historical evidence only.

CircleCI API v3 project resolution and read-only access to the fixed Forge project were verified by the authenticated Preview smoke test; broader live run/job/log/artifact response coverage remains to be verified.
Configured Worker secrets and common credential formats are redacted heuristically; custom or encoded upstream secrets may still appear in logs
Cloudflare built-in rate limiting is approximate and per location, not a strict global limit; dedicated edge WAF hardening remains advisable.
Rate-limit namespace ID must be unique within the user's Cloudflare account
Heuristic log-secret redaction cannot guarantee detection of all custom or encoded credentials

Event inbox is queryable through MCP and browser API but does not push unsolicited messages into an open ChatGPT conversation; a supported notification delivery or polling channel remains to be implemented
CircleCI project webhook registration and automatic Add Webhook ping/check succeeded; an actual CircleCI workflow-completed delivery and end-to-end inbox retrieval remain unverified.

The dashboard can download a bounded JSON report for manual review and attachment; direct ChatGPT-session authentication to the private Browser JSON API remains an unresolved platform integration requirement.

integration_architecture.primary_assistant_access: Private authenticated GET-only Browser JSON API at /api/v1/* using WEB_ACCESS_TOKEN. The existing dashboard can export a bounded JSON report for explicit manual handoff; direct ChatGPT-session authentication remains unverified.
integration_architecture.mcp_requirement: MCP is optional compatibility functionality and is not required as the intended ChatGPT-to-CircleCI access channel.
integration_architecture.credential_separation: WEB_ACCESS_TOKEN and MCP_ACCESS_TOKEN remain separate; neither token is interchangeable or stored in repository files.
integration_architecture.assistant_permissions: Read-only. No CircleCI pipeline/job trigger, rerun, cancel, or settings mutation capability.

ci_execution_policy.scope: Validation of CI Bridge source in Znect All Plugins
ci_execution_policy.provider_boundary: CircleCI remains a read-only external CI provider observed by the Bridge; it is not the executor for validating the Bridge itself.
ci_execution_policy.assistant_access: Read-only inspection of central workflow runs, jobs and run-scoped validation manifest; no workflow dispatch, rerun, cancellation or settings mutation.
